Highly variable within 30km zone; Belarus north corridor higher; plume paths created asymmetric contamination; some areas within 30km below the 37 kBq/m² threshold; some areas outside 30km above 555 kBq/m² (mandatory evacuation)
Northeast corridor higher than southeast; part of main volatile plume trajectory; town of ~10000 evacuated later than 30km zone; now in exclusion zone extension

Hotspot in western direction; some settlements showed higher-than-average contamination; several villages in Narodichi district were evacuated later (1990-1991) after continued monitoring showed high contamination; controversy over adequacy of initial evacuation

Gomel region Belarus: large area >37 kBq/m²; some areas >555 kBq/m²; Belarus bore ~70% of total fallout; Gomel and Mogilev oblasts most contaminated in Belarus; key thyroid dose area in children under 5
Bryansk Russia: most contaminated Russian territory; some areas >555 kBq/m²; contamination drove compensation payments to Russian residents; radiation monitoring in Bryansk ongoing

Northwest plume (0-10 km): ballistic fuel particles (heavy particles, ground-level deposition close to reactor); North-NE plume (50-300 km): volatile aerosols (Cs-137 I-131) lofted high, deposited by rain. This explains why Sr-90/Cs-137 ratio is 10-50x higher in near-field (NW Red Forest) vs far-field (Baltic Scandinavia)
source: OECD-NEA 1996; fuel_particle_contamination_REAL.csv; atmospheric_transport_plume_REAL.csv; UNSCEAR 2008 Annex D
